title.ja: 変更を届ける: CI/CD、OIDC、環境、preview、rollback、drift
title.en: Ship Changes: CI/CD, OIDC, Environments, Previews, Rollback, and Drift

sources.title: Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection
supports: CloudFormation drift detection compares live resource properties with the template; not every resource type or property is covered
Only property values explicitly set in the template or through parameters are compared; default values are not
Resources that do not support drift detection get NOT_CHECKED; a stack with no supported resources is IN_SYNC
Detection on a stack does not detect drift in its nested stacks; run it on the nested stack itself
Detection can run on stacks in CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, and UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED
The caller needs read permission for each resource, plus cloudformation:DetectStackDrift, DetectStackResourceDrift, and BatchDescribeTypeConfigurations
KMSKeyId is never compared; values the service does not return, and Lambda function code, cannot be compared; attachments across stacks may give inaccurate results
DETECTION_FAILED means detection failed for at least one resource; results are available for the others
Stack-level tags are also checked for drift

sources.title: Detect drift on an entire CloudFormation stack
supports: Detection is asynchronous and must be polled to completion
detect-stack-drift returns a detection ID, describe-stack-drift-detection-status reports progress, describe-stack-resource-drifts returns per-resource results
Only one drift detection operation can run on a stack at a time; it may take several minutes
The guide warns to compare the last drift check time with the result timestamps to avoid using stale data

sources.title: Resource type support
supports: Drift detection column is Yes for AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api, Route, Stage, AWS::IAM::Role, AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider, AWS::Lambda::Function, Version, Alias, Permission, and AWS::Logs::LogGroup
Drift detection column is No for AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Integration and AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
AWS::IAM::Policy is not in the table
The table is described as not exhaustive

sources.title: DescribeStackDriftDetectionStatus
supports: DetectionStatus is DETECTION_IN_PROGRESS, DETECTION_FAILED, or DETECTION_COMPLETE; StackDriftStatus is DRIFTED, IN_SYNC, UNKNOWN, or NOT_CHECKED
Response fields used by tools/src/drift/cloudformation-schema.ts

sources.title: DescribeStackResourceDrifts
supports: Returns one result per resource that has been checked; resources not yet checked or not supporting drift detection are not included
Results are paginated with NextToken

sources.title: StackResourceDrift
supports: StackResourceDriftStatus is IN_SYNC, MODIFIED, DELETED, NOT_CHECKED, UNKNOWN, or UNSUPPORTED
Each result carries the Timestamp of when that resource was checked

sources.title: DetectStackDrift
supports: Returns a StackDriftDetectionId; can take up to several minutes; does not descend into nested stacks
The page lists no specific error for a stack that does not exist

sources.title: ListStackResources
supports: Returns every resource of the stack as StackResourceSummary, paginated with NextToken

sources.title: @aws-sdk/client-cloudformation 3.1149.0 (type definitions)
supports: Enum values of StackStatus, StackDriftStatus, StackDriftDetectionStatus, StackResourceDriftStatus, and DifferenceType
StackResourceDriftInformationSummary: resources skipped by ContinueUpdateRollback also have NOT_CHECKED
PropertyDifferences are present only for MODIFIED resources

sources.title: cdk diff
supports: `cdk diff` compares the synthesized template with the deployed template
--method auto (the default) creates a change set with the deploy role and falls back to a template diff; --method template compares templates and uses the lookup role

sources.title: cdk drift
supports: `cdk drift` calls CloudFormation drift detection; `cdk diff` compares templates
--fail returns exit code 1 when drift is detected; no other command-specific option is documented

sources.title: AWS CDK bootstrapping
supports: `cdk bootstrap` deploys the CDKToolkit stack with an asset bucket, an ECR repository, and IAM roles
Each environment (account and Region) must be bootstrapped before deploying into it

sources.title: Bootstrap your environment for use with the AWS CDK
supports: Bootstrapping creates five IAM roles: CloudFormationExecutionRole, DeploymentActionRole, FilePublishingRole, ImagePublishingRole, and LookupRole
Physical names follow cdk-<qualifier>-<description>-<account>-<Region>; the default qualifier is hnb659fds
The deploy role is assumed by the CDK CLI; the CloudFormation execution role is what CloudFormation uses to create resources

sources.title: aws-cdk 2.1145.0 (help output, README, and `cdk bootstrap --show-template`)
supports: Bootstrap template version 32: bucket cdk-<qualifier>-assets-<account>-<region> (versioned, retained on stack deletion, noncurrent versions expire after 30 days), ECR repository cdk-<qualifier>-container-assets-<account>-<region>, five roles, and the SSM parameter /cdk-bootstrap/<qualifier>/version
The CloudFormation execution role gets AdministratorAccess unless --cloudformation-execution-policies or trusted accounts are given
The bootstrap roles trust the account's own principals for sts:AssumeRole; the lookup role has ReadOnlyAccess with a deny on kms:Decrypt
The deploy role's CloudFormation permissions are on Resource *, so it cannot be limited to stacks of one name
Flags of cdk deploy, diff, destroy, drift, rollback, and bootstrap used in examples/20-shipping/src/cdk-args.ts
cdk deploy uses a change set by default and rolls back on failure unless --no-rollback or --express is given
CDK_DISABLE_CLI_TELEMETRY and CDK_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK environment variables; `notices: false` in cdk.json

sources.title: aws-cdk-lib 2.273.0 (type definitions used by chapter 20)
supports: OidcProviderNative creates AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider directly; thumbprints are optional
StackProps.terminationProtection, AppProps.analyticsReporting, Function.currentVersion with currentVersionOptions.removalPolicy
StackProps has no stack policy property

sources.title: Choose how to handle failures when provisioning resources
supports: With rollback disabled, successfully provisioned resources are preserved and failed ones stay in CREATE_FAILED or UPDATE_FAILED
CloudFormation stops at the first failure in each independent provisioning path
A stack in that state is remediated by a retry, an update, or a rollback

sources.title: CreateStack
supports: DisableRollback defaults to false and OnFailure to ROLLBACK
Termination protection is deactivated by default

sources.title: Monitor stack progress
supports: ROLLBACK_COMPLETE exists only after a failed creation, and only a delete can be performed on it
UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED: delete the stack or continue the rollback
During an update with replacement, new resources are created first and old ones deleted in UPDATE_COMPLETE_CLEANUP_IN_PROGRESS
DELETE_FAILED: the stack cannot be updated; delete it again

sources.title: Continue rolling back an update
supports: A stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED cannot be updated, but can be rolled back to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE
Resources skipped while forcing a rollback end up inconsistent with the template

sources.title: Update CloudFormation stacks using change sets
supports: A change set previews how proposed changes affect running resources, including replacement and deletion, before it is executed
A change set does not guarantee that the update will succeed

sources.title: Prevent updates to stack resources
supports: A stack policy applies only during stack updates and is a fail-safe, not access control
Once a stack policy is set, every resource is protected unless explicitly allowed

sources.title: Protect CloudFormation stacks from being deleted
supports: With termination protection, deleting the stack fails and the stack is unchanged; it is disabled by default
Termination protection applies only to attempts to delete the stack; an update that removes a nested stack still deletes it

sources.title: AWS CloudFormation pricing
supports: No additional charge for resource providers in the AWS::* namespace; you pay for the resources created

sources.title: AWS IAM FAQs
supports: IAM is offered at no additional charge

sources.title: CloudFormation resource provider schemas, ap-northeast-1
supports: Read handler permissions of AWS::Lambda::Function, Version, Alias, Permission, AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Api, Route, Stage, AWS::IAM::Role, and AWS::Logs::LogGroup, used for the DriftRole policy
sources.note: That drift detection needs exactly these actions is an inference from the schemas, not a documented statement.

sources.title: AWS service reference: CloudFormation
supports: DescribeStackDriftDetectionStatus and BatchDescribeTypeConfigurations have no resource type, so a policy must use Resource *
DetectStackDrift, DetectStackResourceDrift, DescribeStackResourceDrifts, ListStackResources, and DescribeStacks can be limited to a stack ARN

sources.title: AWS service reference: CloudWatch Logs
supports: DescribeLogGroups, DescribeIndexPolicies, and DescribeResourcePolicies have no resource type

sources.title: Create a role for OpenID Connect federation
supports: For GitHub's provider, IAM rejects a trust policy whose token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub condition is missing or only a wildcard
AWS recommends limiting the condition to specific repositories or branches, and protection rules on GitHub environments used in OIDC policies

sources.title: Create an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in IAM
supports: AWS verifies the provider's JWKS endpoint with its own trusted root CAs and falls back to thumbprints only when it cannot

sources.title: GitHub Actions: OpenID Connect reference
supports: Subject formats: repo:OWNER/REPO:environment:NAME, repo:OWNER/REPO:pull_request (only if the job references no environment), repo:OWNER/REPO:ref:refs/heads/BRANCH
Repositories created after July 15, 2026 use immutable subjects of the form repo:OWNER@OWNER-ID/REPO@REPO-ID:...; older ones keep the previous format unless opted in or renamed
A job needs permissions id-token: write to request the token; that permission grants no write access to anything else

sources.title: GitHub Actions: Configuring OpenID Connect in Amazon Web Services
supports: Provider URL https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com and audience sts.amazonaws.com for the official action
Custom claims for OIDC are not available in AWS
OIDC lets workflows reach AWS without storing AWS credentials as long-lived GitHub secrets

sources.title: GitHub Actions: Secure use reference
supports: Pinning an action to a full-length commit SHA is the only way to use an action as an immutable release

sources.title: GitHub Actions: Events that trigger workflows
supports: Scheduled workflows run on the latest commit of the default branch, can be delayed or dropped under load, and are disabled in public repositories after 60 days without activity
For pull requests from forks, secrets are not passed and GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only

sources.title: GitHub Actions: Deployments and environments
supports: Environments support required reviewers and deployment branch restrictions
On GitHub Free, Pro, and Team, required reviewers are available only for public repositories

sources.title: GitHub Actions billing
supports: Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free in public repositories
Private repositories get a monthly quota of minutes by plan; GitHub Free includes 2,000

sources.title: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials v6.3.0 (action.yml and README at the tagged commit)
supports: v6.3.0 was the latest release on the check date; its tag points at commit e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd
Inputs role-to-assume, aws-region (required), and allowed-account-ids; audience defaults to sts.amazonaws.com; role-duration-seconds defaults to 3600
Session tagging is not used when authenticating with OIDC

supports: v7.0.1, commit 3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1; has a persist-credentials input

supports: v31.11.1, commit 13d8dd58da0234aa297dedd986986ccb8e7f3e24

sources.title: Manage Lambda function versions
supports: A published version's code and most configuration are immutable; deploying code overwrites $LATEST

sources.title: Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias
supports: An alias can split traffic between at most two published versions with the same execution role; a weighted alias cannot point to $LATEST
The split is probabilistic, so low traffic can differ widely from the configured percentage

sources.title: Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy
supports: Predefined canary, linear, and all-at-once configurations exist for Lambda, such as CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Versions & deployments
supports: By default `wrangler deploy` creates a version and deploys it to 100% of traffic in one step
A version captures code, static assets, bindings, and compatibility settings; state in KV, R2, Durable Objects, and D1 is not tracked with versions

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Gradual deployments
supports: A deployment can split traffic between two versions by percentage

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: Rollbacks
supports: `wrangler rollback` creates a new deployment with an earlier version; only the 100 most recent versions can be rolled back to
Resources connected to the Worker are not changed by a rollback, and errors can follow if the structure of data changed between versions

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers: GitHub Actions
supports: The documented setup stores a Cloudflare API token and the account ID as CI secrets for Wrangler

sources.title: cdkd: Drift
supports: Outcome categories and resolution with --accept and --revert
cdkd drift compares cdkd's state with AWS; cdkd diff compares the template with the state

sources.title: cdkd: drift CLI reference
supports: Flags and exit codes of `cdkd drift`
cdkd's state holds a snapshot of every property AWS reported, so drift catches a change to a property never set in the CDK code
CloudFormation's drift detection has nothing to inspect for a stack deployed by cdkd

sources.title: cdkd: Introduction (re-read for chapter 20)
supports: cdkd recommends the AWS CDK CLI for production because CloudFormation provides change sets, stack policies, and the rest of its tooling
One CDK app can be deployed by cdkd to a dev environment and by the AWS CDK CLI to production; a stack can be moved from one tool to the other

sources.title: @go-to-k/cdkd 0.296.28 (help of export and import, provider registry)
supports: `cdkd export` hands a stack to CloudFormation through an IMPORT change set, deletes cdkd's state on success, and aborts if a resource is not importable
`cdkd import --migrate-from-cloudformation` writes cdkd state, sets Retain policies on every resource, then deletes the CloudFormation stack
No dedicated provider is registered for AWS::Lambda::Alias, AWS::Lambda::Version, or AWS::IAM::OIDCProvider; the other types chapter 20 uses have one
sources.note: Read from the installed package's help output and bundled code. Neither command was run.

definition.ja: template を受け取ってリソースを作り、何を作ったかを stack として自分で記録する AWS のサービス。更新に失敗すると、既定では前の状態に戻す。
definition.en: The AWS service that takes a template, creates the resources, and records what it created as a stack. By default it rolls a failed update back.

definition.ja: AWS CDK CLI でデプロイする前に、アカウントとリージョンごとに一度行う準備。CDKToolkit という stack が、asset 用の bucket、ECR repository、5 つの IAM role を作る。cdkd の bootstrap とは別物。
definition.en: The one-time preparation per account and Region before deploying with the AWS CDK CLI. A stack named CDKToolkit creates an asset bucket, an ECR repository, and five IAM roles. Not the same as cdkd's bootstrap.

definition.ja: stack の更新を、実行する前に「何が追加・変更・置き換え・削除されるか」の一覧にしたもの。実行するまで何も変わらない。成功を保証するものではない。
definition.en: A list of what a stack update would add, modify, replace, or delete, made before anything runs. Nothing changes until it is executed, and it does not guarantee success.

definition.ja: あるサービスが発行した署名つきの token で「自分が誰か」を別のサービスに示す標準。この本では、GitHub Actions の job が AWS に入るために使う。
definition.en: A standard for proving who you are to one service with a signed token issued by another. In this book, how a GitHub Actions job gets into AWS.

definition.ja: IAM role に付く「誰がこの role を使えるか」の定義。role に何ができるかを決める権限の policy とは別。
definition.en: The part of an IAM role that says who may use it. Separate from the permission policies that say what the role may do.

definition.ja: OIDC の token に入っている「この token は何のために発行されたか」を表す文字列。GitHub Actions では repository と、branch、environment、pull request のいずれかが入る。
definition.en: The string in an OIDC token that says what the token was issued for. In GitHub Actions it holds the repository and a branch, an environment, or the pull request marker.

definition.ja: 関数のコードと設定の、番号付きの写し。発行したあとは変えられない。発行していない最新の状態は $LATEST と呼ばれる。
definition.en: A numbered copy of a function's code and configuration that cannot change once published. The unpublished latest state is called $LATEST.

definition.ja: version を指す名前つきのポインタ。呼び出す側は alias を呼び、指す先を変えることで版を切り替える。2 つの version に重みを付けて振り分けることもできる。
definition.en: A named pointer to a version. Callers invoke the alias, and moving it switches versions. It can also split traffic between two versions by weight.

definition.ja: 変更を、変更の前の状態に戻すこと。CloudFormation が戻すのは template にあるリソースの設定で、その間に書かれたデータは戻らない。
definition.en: Returning a change to the state before it. CloudFormation puts back the configuration of the resources in the template, not the data written in the meantime.

definition.ja: stack の削除を拒否する設定。解除するまで DeleteStack が失敗する。stack の更新でリソースが消えることは防がない。
definition.en: A setting that refuses to delete a stack: DeleteStack fails until it is turned off. It does not stop an update from removing resources.

definition.ja: pull request ごとに作る、一時的な環境。この本では PR ごとに 1 つの stack。pull request を閉じたら消す前提で作る。
definition.en: A temporary environment created per pull request; in this book, one stack per pull request, made to be deleted when the pull request closes.

definition.ja: 別の stack のリソース（AWS::CloudFormation::Stack）として作られる stack。親の stack で drift を検出しても、中は調べられない。
definition.en: A stack created as a resource (AWS::CloudFormation::Stack) of another stack. Drift detection on the parent does not look inside it.

title.ja: 変更を届ける: stack と CI の role を置いて、誰も呼ばない月
title.en: Shipping: the stack and the CI roles in place, nobody calling for a month

ja: API へのリクエストゼロ。log は失効して保存量ゼロ
CloudFormation は AWS:: の resource type に追加料金なし。IAM の role と OIDC provider は IAM の一部で、追加料金なし
deploy も drift 検出も 0 回
GitHub Actions の料金は AWS の請求ではないので含めていない
en: No requests to the API; logs have expired and nothing is stored
CloudFormation adds no charge for AWS:: resource types; IAM roles and the OIDC provider are part of IAM, at no additional charge
No deploys and no drift detection
GitHub Actions charges are not an AWS bill and are not included

title.ja: 変更を届ける: 1 日 1 回のデプロイを 1 年続けて、asset を一度も片付けない

ja: デプロイのたびにコードが変わり、新しい zip が CDK の asset bucket に 1 つ増える
zip は 1 つ 137 KB（この章の bundle 837 KB を手元で deflate した大きさ。CDK CLI が作る zip の実測ではない）
365 個すべてが残っている月の保存料金。PUT のリクエスト料金は含めていない
en: Every deploy changes the code and adds one new zip to the CDK asset bucket
Each zip is 137 KB (this chapter's 837 KB bundle deflated locally; not a measurement of the zip the CDK CLI makes)
Storage for a month in which all 365 remain; PUT request charges are not included
